meaning: the son of Baldwin
author_comment: As a personal name, so popular in the surname period that it has left its mark deeply indented on all our modern directories; v. Ball, Bodden, Bawcock, &c. Baldwin occurs in Domesday. An aunt of the Conqueror married Baldwin, earl of Flanders; and William himself espoused Matilda, daughter of the fifth Baldwin of that earldom. No wonder Flanders was called 'Baldwin's land' (Freeman's Norm. Conq. i. 601).
source: Hundred Rolls, 1273
record_text: Stephen fil. Baldewyn, co. Camb., 1273. A.
